title: Earthrise was seen only because Apollo 8 was turning at just the right moment

cover.alt: Computer model of the Apollo 8 spacecraft, a grey cylinder with a cone-shaped nose, flying low over the grey cratered surface of the Moon against a black sky.
cover.credit: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio · Public domain

body: On 24 December 1968, Apollo 8 was coming round from the far side of the Moon for the fourth time. Earth had risen over the lunar horizon on each of the three earlier orbits as well, but the spacecraft’s windows faced away from it and the crew never saw it. This time commander Frank Borman was **rolling the ship just as Earth came up**, and it swung into Bill Anders’s side window. Anders called for colour film, Jim Lovell found a roll, and the picture Anders took became the famous Earthrise. In 2013 NASA rebuilt the moment by matching Apollo 8’s automatic photos of the ground, taken every 20 seconds, to 3D maps of the Moon from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.

slides.alt: Computer animation: the Apollo 8 spacecraft, a grey cylinder with a cone-shaped nose, slowly rolls as it flies over the Moon’s grey horizon, and a small blue and white Earth rises from behind the horizon beside it.
slides.caption: Computer model, sped up 3×: Apollo 8 turns as it orbits the Moon on 24 December 1968, and Earth rises over the lunar horizon beyond it.
slides.credit: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio · Public domain · excerpt, cropped, sped up 3×

slides.prompt: Earth had already risen over the Moon on Apollo 8’s three earlier orbits. Why did nobody on board see it?
slides.answer: The windows were facing away from it
slides.detail: Only when commander Frank Borman turned the spacecraft on the fourth orbit did Earth come into view, in Bill Anders’s side window.

slides.text: Oh my God, look at that picture over there! There’s the Earth comin’ up. Wow, is that pretty!
slides.attribution: Bill Anders, on Apollo 8’s onboard recording, 24 December 1968

steps.label: Apollo 8 photographed the ground every 20 s
A modern orbiter mapped that ground in 3D
Matching the two gives the ship’s angle
That shows which window Earth was in, when

slides.question: Anders took the Earthrise photo. Who found him the roll of colour film?
options: Nobody: it was in the camera
slides.explanation: Anders asked for colour film in a hurry, and Lovell found a roll and handed it to him. NASA’s reconstruction calls the picture a group effort.

source.label: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio: Earthrise, the 45th anniversary
